objective: Assess the viability of launching Project SkyNet urban drone delivery in Q4 2026 by evaluating financial projections, consumer acceptance, regulatory compliance, fleet readiness, and external market conditions.
decision_question: Should OmniLogistics proceed with the full launch of Project SkyNet in Q4 2026, or should it delay to address compliance and fleet issues?

Financial Viability.Cost Reduction: Projected 35% reduction in last-mile delivery costs by Q4 2027
Financial Viability.Break-even: 18 months post-launch at 150,000 packages/day across top 5 urban markets

Consumer Adoption.Willingness to Pay: 55% willing to pay up to $2.50 premium for 30-min delivery

Regulatory Compliance.Altitude Limits: 150-300 ft cruising; below 150 ft only during VTOL
Regulatory Compliance.Restricted Zones: No flights over schools during hours, major sporting events, government buildings
Regulatory Compliance.Weight Limit: Max 25 lbs total takeoff weight; Heavy-Lifter v2 exceeds by 2.5 lbs

Fleet Readiness.Mitigation: Recalibrate fleet mix, prioritize Swift-Class, modify dispatch software

External Market Validation.Privacy Mitigation: Shutter outward-facing cameras during final descent

hypotheses.hypothesis: H1: The projected 35% cost reduction and 18-month break-even are achievable given the current capital allocation and market conditions.
H2: Consumer concerns about noise and privacy can be sufficiently mitigated by deploying Whisper-Prop and camera shuttering, maintaining the 68% acceptance rate.
H3: The regulatory weight limit (25 lbs) will force a fleet mix shift to Swift-Class drones, potentially reducing payload capacity and affecting delivery volume targets.
H4: External market benchmarks (e.g., competitor drone delivery costs, regulatory trends) will validate or challenge the internal financial projections.
H5: The 150,000 packages/day threshold is feasible across top 5 urban markets given consumer willingness to pay and operational constraints.
